title: riskell-setup --doctor --json
description: One health report. Contracted: the schema number (this file's $id), the ten sections in the order a person meets a broken bar, a check's `id` (which is the contract; its label and detail are prose), each check's severity and where the fact came from, the counts, the first failing check's id, and whether the running bars answered. Read-only: nothing here is written and no word that changes anything is sent. The report's `exit` is the same number the run returns, and a report with a failed check is still a report, so both 0 and 1 are a good run. Checked by Tests/cli/contract.sh.

schema.description: The report's own number, bumped when a key moves or changes meaning. This file is named for it: $id is "1".

generatedAt.description: When the report was made, UTC to the second.

macos.description: The version the check ran on, or an empty string when it could not be read.

running.description: What launchd says about the login agent. Null fields mean it is not installed or not running.

version.description: The version the installed app reports, not the one in this checkout.

socket.description: The event socket, with the home folder cut to ~/.

ok.description: No check failed. A warn does not clear it.

exit.description: The number the run returns: 0 when ok, else 1.

sections.description: In the order a person meets a broken bar, ending in the verdict row, which repeats the counts.

id.description: Stable across versions: build, system, install, files, running, window manager, permissions, gestures, log, verdict.

status.description: The worst row in the section; an empty section is ok.

id.description: The contract, and the only stable name here: build.binary in every version. `detail` is not.

label.description: What a person reads. Display only.

severity.description: info is nothing to check here, never a problem.

detail.description: Prose, and it carries this machine's paths: print it, do not parse it.

fix.description: The next command to run. Always there for a fail, otherwise optional.

source.description: Where the fact came from: probed here, asked of the running bars, read from a file, or read from launchd.

app.description: The running bars' own answer, as they sent it: the app's schema, not this one. `reachable` comes first and decides the rest, so a report without a running bar says so instead of looking silent. Everything else here is the app's payload and is not part of this contract.

schema.description: AppStatus.schema: the app's own number, which moves on its own.

atoms.description: How many atoms the bars hold.

bars.description: The bars that are on: left, right, top, bottom.

then.description: The bars answered, so the answer is all there.

files.description: What the files hold. A config's values are never carried, only the key names, so a report can be sent to a maintainer.

config.$comment: A JSON file the report reads: `valid` and `keys` are absent while the file does not exist.

path.description: With the home folder cut to ~/.

keys.description: Key names, sorted: never a value.

answers.description: It answered the `doctor` word: the difference between a stale socket file and a running bar.

gapsBackup.description: riskell saved the outer gaps before writing its own.

firstFailure.description: The id of the first failing check, or null when nothing failed: the one thing to read first.
